sentences.text: Note 12. 05.12.2024 CGR, J I.A.No.1 of 2008 This application is filed to condone delay of 225 days in filing the review petition seeking review of the order in Judgment dated 04.04.2007 in W.P.No.24157 of 1999.
No Counter is filed opposing the same.
Even on last hearing none appeared.
Heard the learned Assistant Government Pleader and no representation for the respondents in the application.

The learned Assistant Government Pleader would submit that the writ petition came to be allowed based on the letter bearing RC No.582/2000 (Inam) dated 24.06.2006 by which officer viz., Ms.C.V Ramani, Special Deputy Tahsildar (Inams) has confirmed that the 1st petitioner was enjoying the subject property and the same having been considered by this Court, allowed the writ petition holding that the 1st petitioner was entitled for ex-gratia.

Immediately after the judgment was passed, the office of the respondents i.e., the Special Deputy Collector, (lands acquisition), NTPC,
Unit I, Visakhapatnam, verified the records and came to know that the alleged letter dated 24.06.2006 was issued in collusion with the 1st petitioner and therefore has immediately approached the office of Government Pleader to file review petition, basing on which, the present review came to be filed.

In this process, there is a delay of 225 days and as the above said letter was a clear act of fraud, it is stated that in the interest of the State and the larger public interest, the delay may be condoned.
There is no opposition to the above said submission.

Having considered the above submissions and the reasons mentioned in the affidavit filed in support of the application, this Court is satisfied that though there is a delay of 225 days in preferring the review, having regard to the fact that there is an element of allegation fraud, which is prima-facie pleaded, and in view of the larger public interest, besides considering that the departmental action against the officer is recommended immediately, delay is condoned.

sentences.text: The present review is preferred by the review petitioners/State seeking review of the Judgment dated 04.04.2007 passed in W.P.No.24157 of 1999.
Heard the learned Assistant Government Pleader for the review petitioners and there is no representation for the respondents/writ petitioners.

Initially, the writ petition was filed to declare GOMs No.239, Revenue (Assignment-I) Department,
dated 22.03.1999 and G.O.Ms NO.711, (Assignment- I) Department, dated 05.10.1999 as illegal,
arbitrary and to set aside the same and consequently, to direct the respondents to pay the entire compensation amount to the petitioners in respect of the lands in R.S.Nos.460/2, 460/3, 462P,
467/1, 2 and 3 and 468 admeasuring Ac.5.90 cents, Ac.1.81 cents, Ac.6.74 cents, Ac.4.10 cents and Ac.7.55 cents, respectively situated at Devada Village, Pedagantyada Mandal, Visakhapatnam District.
The said writ petition was preferred by the two petitioners viz., NSR Murthy and G.Suryanarayana Reddy.

However, the 2nd petitioner, G.Suryanarayana Reddy, later withdrew the writ petition and the 1st petitioner has filed for amendment of writ prayer, whereby he has confined the writ petition claiming ex-gratia to him at the rate of 35% as entitled under G.O.Ms No.239 dated 22.03.1999 and G.O.Ms No.711 dated 05.10.1999, which prayer was allowed on 24.02.2004.

The writ petitioners claim in the writ petition is that they have purchased lands in R.S.Nos.460/2,
460/3, and 462P admeasuring Ac.5.90 cents, Ac.1.81 cents and Ac.6.74 cents, respectively situated at Devada Village, Pedagantyada Mandal, Visakhapatnam from Mokhasa Inamdars through registered relinquishment deed/sale deed 15.10.1994 and since the date of purchase
, they claimed to have been in possession and enjoyment of the same.
Considering the aforesaid purchase, it is claimed that the Special Deputy Tahsildar (Inams), Revenue Department, Visakhapatnam, granted Ryatowari patta in favour of the 1st petitioner.
While so, the 3rd respondent proposed to acquire the aforesaid lands for setting up of a power project by Hinduja Power Corporation and National Thermal Power Corporation.

As there were certain disputes with respect to the status of the lands those are to be acquired, on one side being claimed by the Government, on the other side third party claims are made and besides that subject lands were also under encroachment by 3 rd parties, the Government of Andhra Pradesh issued G.O.Ms No.239 dated 22.03.1999 and G.O.MS No.711 dated 05.10.1999, settling respective claims by various parties, inter-alia proposing that the compensation for the said land to be acquired shall be paid to Government at the rate of 30%, 35% to the Waqf board and remaining 35% to the occupants, either be purchasers or encroachers.
In this view of the matter, the 2nd petitioner claimed to be in possession of the property in terms of the aforesaid purchase and claimed for the compensation at the rate of 35%.

The Government has filed the counter interalia stating that the land said to be acquired, in particular those claimed by the 1 st petitioner are classified as Government lands and recorded as assessed waste as per Section 2(a) of Inams (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1956, and the same have been vested with the Government and the whole Devada village was Inam Village granted for maintenance of Dargah, situated at Visakhapatnam.

sentences.text: When the writ petition taken up for hearing, this Court while considering the proceedings bearing RC.No.582/2000 (Inam) dated 24.06.2006 which were issued apparently based on the representation made by the 1st petitioner holding that he was declared to be enjoyer of the lands in possession, has allowed the writ petition declaring that the 1st petitioner was eligible to draw ex-gratia at the rate of 35% in terms of the GOs referred above.

It was also directed that the ex-gratia be disbursed along with interest accrued from the date of deposit in the Court till the date of payment and complete the said exercise within four (4) weeks from the date of receipt of the copy of the order.

The learned Assistant Government Pleader would submit that there is an apparent error on the face of the order dated 04.04.2007 inasmuch as though in the counter filed, it was categorically stated that the subject land vested with the Government and that 1st petitioner was not in possession and enjoyment of the same, which even recorded in the impugned order under review, merely basing on the letter bearing RC.No.582/2000 (Inam) dated 24.06.2006 alleged to have been issued by the then Special Deputy Tahsildar (Inams), Office of Revenue Divisional Officer, Visakhapatnam,
confirming the enjoyment of the 1st petitioner, the relief in the writ petition came to be granted and infact such letter was issued by then then Officer Viz., Ms.C.V.Ramani, without any basis and contrary to the reports of her predecessors dated 03.04.2000 and 07.09.2000 and even the District Collector addressed letter vide RC.No.1356/1998/E3 dated 19.12.2007 to the Government (Vigilance) Department, Secretariat recommending to initiate disciplinary action against the said lady officer for issuing the alleged letter bearing RC.No.582/2000 (Inam) dated 24.06.2006 which is clearly demonstrable as fraudulent act and hence prays to review the order.
None appeared for the respondents.
No counter is filed in the review application.
Perused the record.

Apparently, the writ petition came to be disposed based on proceedings bearing RC.No.582/2000 (Inam) dated 24.06.2006 issued by the then Special Deputy Tahildar (Inams), Office of RDO,
Visakhapatnam, without going into the merits of the matter whereby the Government had specifically pleaded in the counter that the subject lands are Government lands as it has been vested with the Government under the Provisions of Inams (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act,
1956, and that the 1st petitioner was never in possession of the same nor can be treated as an encroacher.

sentences.text: Even the said submission has been recorded in the order under review, however the same was not dealt with and no specific finding has been recorded.

This Court feels that the Government has taken a substantial stand and also alleged that the Ryotwari patta produced by the 1st petitioner was not genuine and also there were reports issued by the office of Special Deputy Tahsildar (Inams) dated 03.04.2000 and 07.09.2000, besides the recommendation of the District Collector dated 19.12.2007 to initiate disciplinary action against the officer who has issued the aforesaid letter dated 24.06.2006, which confirmed possession and enjoyment of the 1st petitioner,
therefore, to meet ends of justice, this Court finds that the review requires to be allowed and N.S.R.Murthy And Another vs Ap/Secy/Revassignment/Hyd And 2 Ors on 5 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156300180/
